rules.explanation: The first heading may use any depth. A later heading may descend by any amount but may not increase by more than one level at a time, because a skipped level makes the document outline ambiguous for readers and assistive technology. The diagnostic covers the whole heading node, marker included.
rules.fixes: The rule reports a manual suggestion. The correct heading level is a prose decision, so no edit is applied automatically and neither `--fix` nor `--unsafe-fixes` changes the heading.
limitations: Only headings with a locatable node span are reported; a heading the extractor cannot map to source bytes is skipped.
The rule compares depth only: it does not enforce a document outline or a maximum depth, and a document may begin at any level.
Configuration, per-file ignores, and suppression directives can stop a finding; static metadata does not describe effective enablement for a particular file.

rules.explanation: Two or more identical alphabetic tokens separated only by spaces or tabs are reported as a repeated run. Comparison is exact, so `the the` is a run and `The the` is not. A run never crosses markup, a region boundary, a line break, or a synthetic region, and inline code is excluded. The `TOKENS` capability is supplied by the builtin pack's in-process tokenizer; no NLP model or external provider is loaded.
rules.fixes: The rule may propose an unsafe edit that removes the repeated suffix. Apply it only with `stilyagi check --fix --unsafe-fixes`; `--fix` alone skips it, and the `lint.fixable` policy still decides whether the code may contribute an edit. Review the diff before applying it, because a deliberate repetition such as `had had` is removed just as an accidental one is.
limitations: Matching is exact and adjacent: `the the` is a run, but `the plan the plan` is not because other words intervene.
A deliberate repetition is reported the same way as an accidental one, and the unsafe edit cannot tell them apart.
Only headings, paragraphs, and table cells are inspected; inline code, code blocks, and unsupported regions are not.
Synthetic segment text that cannot be mapped to source bytes is not editable, so no edit is offered for it.

rules.explanation: Every configured term is matched against whole alphabetic tokens, so `obviously` never matches inside `unobviously`. The `TOKENS` capability is supplied by the builtin pack's in-process tokenizer; no NLP model or external provider is loaded. When `case_sensitive` is false, which is the default, both the configured term and the token are compared with Unicode `casefold()`; when it is true, the exact spelling is compared. Duplicate terms coalesce under the chosen comparison. The rule is opt-in and does nothing until terms are configured.
rules.fixes: The rule offers no fix. Choosing a replacement for a banned term is editorial, so no edit is planned and `--fix` leaves the source unchanged.
limitations: Only headings, paragraphs, and table cells are inspected; code blocks, inline code, link destinations, and frontmatter are not.

Matching is whole-token only, but hyphens, punctuation, and digits are token boundaries: a term can match one word inside a hyphenated or punctuated form. Use an exact context check when that is too broad.
The opposite editorial policy, requiring a term rather than banning it, is not supported; no inverse rule or option exists in this slice.
Neither case mode promises locale-aware matching or Unicode normalization; use `case_sensitive = true` when exact spelling matters.
